title: AugServe: Adaptive Request Scheduling for Augmented Large Language Model Inference Serving
technique: state-aware request scheduling (value-density priority over predicted space-time cost, handling paused/external-call requests) plus dynamic batch-level token budget

optimized_metrics.evidence: Our goal is to maximize goodput in augmented LLM inference, accounting for both request service rates and queuing delays.
We present AugServe, an efficient augmented LLM inference serving framework that mitigates request queuing latency and improves effective throughput under external-call-augmented workloads.
SLOs are set as TTFT<1s and normalized latency<10× single-iteration time.

headline_claim.text: AugServe achieves 6.5× and 4.7× higher effective throughput than vLLM and INFERCEPT, respectively.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the system’s efficiency is best characterized by effective throughput (or goodput), defined as the volume of requests processed per unit time that successfully satisfy these SLO requirements
metric_definitions.notes: Unit req/s; a request counts only if it meets both TTFT and normalized-latency SLOs. Abstract says 6.5x/4.7x; §6.1 text says goodput geometric mean 7.5x vs vLLM, 5.7x vs INFERCEPT (inconsistent between abstract/intro and §6.1 in this version).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: goodput (number of SLO-satisfying requests per unit time)
normalized latency (end-to-end latency divided by output length)
TTFT reflects the queuing delay before the first token is generated.
SLO attainment (i.e., the fraction of requests meeting SLOs, Appendix D.8)

slo_spec: TTFT < 1 s and normalized latency < 10x single-iteration time, following prior work (Gao et al. 2025; Wu et al. 2023); goodput = SLO-satisfying requests per unit time
load_regime: request-rate sweep; W1 Poisson arrivals over 30 min; W2 Gamma arrivals with varying CV
tradeoff_acknowledged: Throughput vs delay-awareness controlled by beta in the scheduling value; too small or too large token budgets hurt goodput (Table 1); SJF better than FCFS but suboptimal at high load.
workloads: INFERCEPT dataset and ToolBench (augmented LLM requests with external API calls); Poisson and Gamma arrivals
extractor_notes: Request-level metrics (TTFT, normalized latency of a single augmented request that pauses on API calls); no program-level JCT. TTFT interplay with pauses not specified (TTFT is first token of the request, i.e. before any call). Abstract vs §6.1 goodput multipliers disagree (6.5x/4.7x vs 7.5x/5.7x). Quality not measured.
